statement: A top-5 developer reports AI systems did >= 50% of code or experiments in a frontier training project (technical report or system card; by 2028-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not met in 2024. The strongest public figure was company-wide, not project-specific: a top-5 developer's CEO said more than a quarter of all new code at the company was AI-generated and then human-reviewed (Oct). Independent R&D benchmarks found agents competitive with experts only on short (2-hour) ML engineering tasks (Nov). A start-up demonstrated end-to-end automated generation of small ML papers (~USD 15 each; Aug), far from a frontier training project.

items.summary: A non-top-5 AI start-up with academic partners released a system claimed to automate the full research cycle (ideas, code, experiments, paper) for small ML studies at ~USD 15 per paper, acknowledging flaws. Not a frontier training project; precursor only.
items.detail: Sakana AI with Oxford (Foerster Lab) and UBC (Clune, Lu), 'The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery', 2024-08-13.

items.summary: A top-5 developer's CEO stated on an earnings call that more than a quarter of all new code at the company is generated by AI, then reviewed and accepted by engineers. Company-wide share, self-reported, below 50% and not specific to a frontier training project.
items.detail: Alphabet Q3 2024 earnings call, CEO Sundar Pichai's remarks (blog.google transcript; also abc.xyz IR transcript). Page opened via web_extract; quoted sentence confirmed in search snippet of the same page.

items.summary: Independent AI R&D benchmark: frontier agents beat human experts on ML research-engineering tasks at a 2-hour budget but fell behind at longer budgets; one agent wrote a GPU kernel faster than the best human. Capability for doing most work on a real frontier project not shown.
items.detail: METR RE-Bench, 2024-11-22 (o1-preview prefix-sum kernel 0.64 ms vs best human 0.67 ms).
